---
engine: markdown
title: "Set a table right to left"
subtitle: "The same table, mirrored with the writing direction."
description: "Keisen aligns cells to start and end rather than to a side, so a table under a right-to-left text direction mirrors with the text."
---

Nothing in the table is written for one direction.
Cells align to `start` and `end` rather than to a side, so the same table built once and set twice mirrors with the text around it.

```{typst}
//| file: ../../tests/visual/direction.typ
//| echo: true
//| alt: "The same table twice: first in left-to-right text with the stub first and amounts on the right, then in right-to-left text with the columns in the opposite order, the stub last, text against the right edge and amounts against the left, still lined up on their decimal separators."
```

The columns run the other way and the stub sits last, because Typst lays a table out along the writing direction.
Inferred alignment follows: text goes to the start of its cell and numbers to the end, whichever side those are on.

A number is the exception, and deliberately so.
Its digits, separator and any exponent are pinned left to right, since a number reads the same way in every script.
